classes.label: Phenethylamine
classes.description: **Phenethylamines** consist of a benzene ring connected to an amino group by a two-carbon ethyl chain (the phenethylamine, or phenylethylamine, backbone). Members of the class are produced by adding substituents to the aromatic ring, the side-chain carbons, or the amine nitrogen; common ring substitutions include methoxy groups, as seen in the mescaline-type and 2C series. This simple backbone is the structural parent of several other classes here, including amphetamines, cathinones and the 2C compounds.

classes.label: Amphetamine
classes.description: **Amphetamines** are phenethylamines that carry an extra methyl group on the alpha carbon, the side-chain carbon next to the amine, giving the alpha-methylphenethylamine backbone. Members vary by substituents on the benzene ring (such as the methylenedioxy bridge of MDMA), on the amine nitrogen (an N-methyl group converts amphetamine into methamphetamine), and by that alpha-methyl branch which distinguishes the class from unbranched phenethylamines. The alpha-methyl group is the defining structural marker of the family.

classes.label: Tryptamine
classes.description: **Tryptamines** are built around an indole ring system, a benzene ring fused to a five-membered nitrogen-containing pyrrole ring, with an aminoethyl (ethylamine) side chain attached at the indole's 3-position. Individual members differ mainly in what is attached to the terminal amine nitrogen (for example dimethyl groups as in DMT) and in substituents on the indole ring, such as a hydroxyl or phosphoryloxy group at the 4-position (psilocin and psilocybin) or a methoxy group at the 5-position. The serotonin molecule shares this same tryptamine backbone, which is why the class is often described in relation to it.

classes.label: Cathinone
classes.description: **Cathinones** are the beta-keto analogues of amphetamines: they share the alpha-methylphenethylamine backbone but add a ketone (carbonyl) group at the beta carbon of the side chain, the carbon adjacent to the benzene ring. Aside from this beta-keto group, members differ in the same ways amphetamines do, through ring substituents and groups on the amine nitrogen (for example the methylenedioxy ring and N-methyl of methylone). The presence of the beta-keto group is what defines the class and relates each cathinone to its corresponding amphetamine.

classes.label: Benzodiazepine
classes.description: **Benzodiazepines** share a fused bicyclic core in which a benzene ring is joined to a seven-membered diazepine ring, a ring containing two nitrogen atoms (the classic 1,4-diazepine arrangement). Most members additionally carry a second pendant phenyl ring and varied substituents around the core, such as chlorine, nitro or fluorine groups, which distinguish individual compounds. Many also have a fused triazole or imidazole ring added to the diazepine, producing the triazolo- and imidazo-benzodiazepine subgroups.

classes.label: Arylcyclohexylamine
classes.description: **Arylcyclohexylamines** are built from a cyclohexane (six-membered carbon) ring that carries two key groups on the same carbon: an aromatic aryl ring and an amine. The amine is often part of a second ring, such as the piperidine of PCP or, in ketamine, an N-methylamino group paired with an additional ketone on the cyclohexane and a chlorine on the aryl ring. Members differ by the choice of aryl ring, the type of amine, and substituents added to the cyclohexane.

classes.label: Lysergamide
classes.description: **Lysergamides** are amides of lysergic acid, a complex four-ring fused structure (a tetracyclic ergoline) that contains an indole system embedded within additional rings, giving the molecule a rigid, locked geometry. The defining feature of the class is a carboxamide group at the ergoline 8-position; LSD, for instance, carries a diethylamide there, while other members swap in different amine groups on that amide. Because the ergoline scaffold rigidly holds a tryptamine-like unit in place, lysergamides can be viewed as conformationally constrained relatives of the tryptamines.

classes.label: 2C-x
classes.description: **2C-x** compounds are a subfamily of phenethylamines defined by two methoxy groups on the benzene ring at the 2- and 5-positions, with a variable substituent at the 4-position that gives each member its name (the "x"), such as bromine in 2C-B or an ethyl group in 2C-E. The "2C" label refers to the two-carbon chain between the ring and the amino group, which is left unbranched (unlike the amphetamines, which add a methyl branch). They are essentially the ring-substituted 2,5-dimethoxy phenethylamines, with the corresponding alpha-methyl versions forming the related DOx amphetamine series.

classes.label: NBOMe (x-NBOMe)
classes.description: **N-benzyl phenethylamines (NBOMe)** are 2C-x phenethylamines in which a benzyl group bearing a methoxy substituent (an N-2-methoxybenzyl group, hence "NBOMe") has been attached to the amine nitrogen. The core therefore keeps the 2,5-dimethoxy benzene ring and 4-position substituent of the parent 2C compound (for example 25I-NBOMe derives from 2C-I), with the added N-benzyl arm being the distinguishing structural change. This N-benzyl addition is the single feature that separates the class from the plain 2C-x phenethylamines.

classes.label: Morphinan
classes.description: **Morphinans** are built on a fused tetracyclic (four-ring) carbon skeleton derived from the morphine framework, including a partially hydrogenated phenanthrene core with a nitrogen-containing ring bridged across it. Members differ by which oxygen-bearing groups (hydroxyl, methoxy or ketone) sit on the rings, by the presence or absence of an oxygen bridge linking two rings, and by the substituent on the nitrogen. Morphine, codeine and many semi-synthetic opioids are variations on this shared rigid morphinan scaffold.

classes.label: Pyrrolidine
classes.description: **Substituted pyrrolidines (pyrrolidinophenones)** are cathinone-type molecules in which the amine nitrogen is incorporated into a five-membered pyrrolidine ring. They retain the cathinone framework, a benzene ring linked to an alpha-methyl side chain bearing a beta-keto group, but the terminal amine is replaced by this pyrrolidine ring, as seen in alpha-PVP and MDPV. Members vary by ring substituents, by the length of the alkyl chain on the side chain, and by whether a methylenedioxy bridge is present on the aromatic ring.

classes.label: Cannabinoid
classes.description: **Cannabinoids** are a structurally diverse group; the classical (phytocannabinoid) members share a dibenzopyran-type framework in which an aromatic ring bearing a hydroxyl and a long alkyl (pentyl) chain is fused to an oxygen-containing pyran ring and a carbocyclic terpene-derived ring, as in THC and CBD. Synthetic cannabinoids often abandon this scaffold entirely, instead linking various core groups (such as indole or indazole rings) through amide or ester linkers to assorted tail and head groups. What unites the class is shared activity at cannabinoid receptors rather than a single common skeleton, so it spans several distinct structural families.

classes.label: Benzofuran
classes.description: **Benzofurans** are based on the benzofuran ring system, a benzene ring fused to a five-membered oxygen-containing furan ring. In the psychoactive members this fused ring system replaces the methylenedioxyphenyl portion of compounds like MDA/MDMA, with an aminopropyl side chain attached, as in 5-APB and 6-APB. They are therefore close structural relatives of the amphetamines and phenethylamines, differing mainly by the benzofuran ring in place of a simpler substituted benzene.

classes.label: Anilidopiperidine
classes.description: **Anilidopiperidines (fentanyls)** are organized around a piperidine ring (a six-membered ring with one nitrogen) that bears an anilide group, an amide linking the ring to a phenyl-bearing aniline, which gives the class its name. The piperidine nitrogen typically carries a phenethyl arm, and individual members differ by substituents on the rings and by the acyl group of the amide, as in the methyl-substituted carfentanil or the thiophene ring of sufentanil. The aniline-amide attached to a substituted piperidine is the defining structural motif.

classes.label: Phenidate
classes.description: **Phenidates** are built around a structure that joins a phenyl (benzene) ring and a six-membered, nitrogen-containing piperidine ring to a central carbon, which also carries an ester group, formally esters of phenyl(piperidin-2-yl)acetic acid. Methylphenidate is the prototype, with a methyl ester; other members vary the ester group, the aromatic ring substituents, or the piperidine, as in ethylphenidate and isopropylphenidate. The phenyl–piperidine–ester arrangement is the consistent structural signature of the class.

classes.label: Gabapentinoid
classes.description: **Gabapentinoids** are structural analogues of the neurotransmitter GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid), built around the same short amino-acid chain but with a lipophilic group added at the 3-position of that backbone. In gabapentin the addition is a cyclohexane ring fused onto the chain, while in pregabalin it is an isobutyl branch, making both 3-substituted GABA derivatives. This shared GABA backbone with a bulky lipophilic substituent is the structural thread linking the class.

classes.label: Piperazine
classes.description: **Piperazines** are defined by the piperazine ring, a six-membered ring containing two nitrogen atoms positioned opposite each other (the 1,4 arrangement). Psychoactive members carry substituents on one or both nitrogens, broadly splitting into benzylpiperazines, which attach a benzyl group as in BZP, and phenylpiperazines, which attach a phenyl ring directly as in mCPP and TFMPP, often with halogen or trifluoromethyl groups on that ring. The shared two-nitrogen piperazine ring with an attached aromatic group is the structural hallmark of the class.

classes.label: MDxx
classes.description: **MDxx** compounds are ring-substituted phenethylamines and amphetamines built around a methylenedioxy bridge — a small ring fused across the 3,4-positions of the benzene ring — which is the structural feature the "MD" prefix points to. MDMA, MDA, and MDEA share this 3,4-methylenedioxy phenyl group attached to an alpha-methyl (amphetamine) side chain, differing mainly in the group on the amine nitrogen. The methylenedioxy ring is what distinguishes the family from the plain amphetamines and phenethylamines it is otherwise derived from.

classes.label: Barbiturate
classes.description: **Barbiturates** are built on a barbituric acid core: a six-membered ring containing two nitrogen atoms and three carbonyl (keto) groups, formed by combining urea with a malonic acid unit. Individual members carry two substituents on the central carbon of that ring — typically alkyl, aryl, or allyl groups — which distinguish compounds such as phenobarbital and pentobarbital. The thiobarbiturates are a close variant in which one ring oxygen is replaced by a sulfur atom.

classes.label: Racetam
classes.description: **Racetams** share a five-membered 2-pyrrolidinone ring — a pyrrolidine ring carrying a single carbonyl (keto) group — which is the structure their "-racetam" suffix refers to. Members differ by the groups attached to that ring, most often an acetamide on the ring nitrogen as in piracetam, plus further additions that give relatives such as aniracetam and oxiracetam. The 2-pyrrolidinone nucleus is the consistent backbone uniting the family.

classes.label: Aminoindane
classes.description: **Aminoindanes** are conformationally rigid analogues of amphetamine in which the flexible side chain is locked into a ring: the indane system, a benzene ring fused to a five-membered carbocyclic ring, carries the amino group on that saturated ring (typically the 2-position). Members differ by substituents on the aromatic ring, including the methylenedioxy bridge of MDAI or a halogen as in 5-IAI, and by N-alkylation. Tying the amphetamine backbone into the indane ring is what defines and rigidifies the class.

classes.label: Diarylethylamine
classes.description: **Diarylethylamines** are dissociative-type molecules built on a two-carbon ethylamine chain that bears two aromatic aryl rings, one on each of the two carbons (the 1,2-diarylethylamine arrangement). The amine is frequently incorporated into a ring such as piperidine or pyrrolidine, as in diphenidine, or left as a simple N-ethyl group, as in ephenidine, and ring substituents like methoxy groups distinguish members such as methoxphenidine. They are close structural cousins of the arylcyclohexylamines, achieving a similar aryl-plus-amine layout using an open two-aryl ethyl chain rather than a cyclohexane ring.

classes.label: Tropane
classes.description: **Tropane alkaloids** are defined by the tropane ring system, a bicyclic structure in which a nitrogen-containing bridge spans a seven-membered carbon ring, formally a fused pyrrolidine and piperidine sharing two carbons with an N-methyl bridge. Members carry various groups esterified or attached to this bicyclic core; cocaine, for instance, adds a benzoyl ester and a methyl ester, while atropine and scopolamine attach a tropic-acid ester. The rigid bridged tropane skeleton is the common structural feature uniting the class.

classes.label: Aminorex
classes.description: **Aminorex** compounds are organized around a 2-amino-oxazoline ring: a five-membered ring containing both an oxygen and a nitrogen, bearing an amino group, with a phenyl ring attached. Members such as aminorex and 4-methylaminorex differ by substituents on that phenyl ring or on the oxazoline ring itself. The amino-aryl-oxazoline arrangement defines the class and relates it structurally to the broader phenethylamine stimulants.

classes.label: Amine
classes.description: Compounds built around a basic nitrogen atom bonded to alkyl or aryl groups. The amine is the broadest structural family in psychopharmacology: nearly every classical stimulant, psychedelic, opioid, and depressant scaffold on this site descends from it.

classes.label: Arylalkylamine
classes.description: Amines in which an aromatic ring is joined to the amino group through a short carbon chain. This umbrella covers the phenethylamines, tryptamines, and their many descendants — the structural core of most monoaminergic psychoactives.

classes.label: Thiopropamine
classes.description: Amphetamine analogues in which the benzene ring is replaced by a thiophene ring, exemplified by methiopropamine (MPA). The sulfur-for-carbon ring swap is a classic bioisosteric substitution.

classes.label: Scaline (3,5-dimethoxyphenethylamine)
classes.description: Phenethylamines carrying methoxy groups at the 3- and 5-positions with a variable 4-position substituent — the mescaline analogues. Positional isomers of the 2C-x family, they are predominantly serotonergic psychedelics.

classes.label: 3C-x (3,5-dimethoxyamphetamine)
classes.description: The α-methylated homologues of the scalines: amphetamines bearing the 3,5-dimethoxy pattern, such as 3C-E and 3C-P. They relate to the scalines exactly as the DOx series relates to the 2C-x series.

classes.label: DOx (2,5-dimethoxyamphetamine)
classes.description: Amphetamines carrying the 2,5-dimethoxy substitution pattern with a variable 4-position substituent — the α-methylated homologues of the 2C-x series. Long-acting, potent serotonergic psychedelics such as DOM, DOI, and DOB.

classes.label: N-benzylphenethylamine (x-NBx)
classes.description: Phenethylamines extended with a benzyl group on the amine nitrogen, which dramatically increases serotonin 5-HT2A receptor affinity. The family divides by the benzyl ring's 2-position substituent into the NBOMe, NBOH, NBF, and related series.

classes.label: NBF (x-NBF)
classes.description: N-benzylphenethylamines with a fluorine at the benzyl 2-position, such as 25I-NBF. Bioisosteres of the NBOMe series with generally somewhat reduced receptor affinity.

classes.label: NBOH (x-NBOH)
classes.description: N-benzylphenethylamines with a hydroxyl at the benzyl 2-position, such as 25B-NBOH and 25C-NBOH. Potent 5-HT2A agonists closely related to the NBOMes.

classes.label: NB3OMe (x-NB3OMe)
classes.description: Positional isomers of the NBOMes with the methoxy group moved to the benzyl 3-position, which markedly lowers 5-HT2A affinity relative to the 2-position parents.

classes.label: NB4OMe (x-NB4OMe)
classes.description: Positional isomers of the NBOMes with the methoxy group at the benzyl 4-position; like the NB3OMe series, substantially less potent than the 2-methoxy parents.

classes.label: Benzeneacetamide
classes.description: Acetamide-bridged aryl compounds that include most of the Upjohn 'U-series' opioids beyond U-47700 itself. Structurally they sit between the phenethylamine and benzamide families.

classes.label: 2-Benzylpiperidine
classes.description: Amphetamine relatives in which the amine nitrogen is incorporated into a piperidine ring attached at the benzylic position. The phenidates, including methylphenidate, are its best-known branch.

classes.label: Phenylmorpholine
classes.description: Amphetamines cyclized into a morpholine ring, as in phenmetrazine and 3-FPM. Predominantly dopaminergic–noradrenergic stimulants.

classes.label: Phenylpropylamine
classes.description: Arylalkylamines with a three-carbon chain between ring and nitrogen, one carbon longer than the phenethylamines. Includes the atypical opioid analgesics tramadol and tapentadol.

classes.label: Diphenylpropylamine
classes.description: Phenylpropylamines carrying a second aryl ring, the scaffold of the methadone family of full opioid agonists.

classes.label: Benzylamine
classes.description: Arylalkylamines with a single carbon between the aromatic ring and the nitrogen. A small umbrella that covers the benzamide opioids, the benzylpiperazines, and (by one lineage) the arylcyclohexylamines.

classes.label: Benzamide
classes.description: Compounds built on an amide-linked benzene ring, most prominently the 'U-series' opioid U-47700 and its relatives.

classes.label: Quinazolinone
classes.description: Bicyclic ketone-bearing heterocycles exemplified by methaqualone and etaqualone — sedative-hypnotics chemically unrelated to the benzodiazepines despite similar effects.

classes.label: Cycloalkylamine
classes.description: Amines attached to a saturated carbon ring rather than a flat aromatic one. Its principal psychoactive branch is the arylcyclohexylamine dissociatives.

classes.label: Ibogalog (hexahydroazepinoindole)
classes.description: Simplified analogues of the iboga alkaloids built on the hexahydroazepinoindole core, such as ibogainalog and tabernanthalog, alongside ibogaine itself.

classes.label: β-Carboline
classes.description: Tricyclic tryptamine relatives formed by ring closure between the indole and the ethylamine chain. The harmala alkaloids (harmine, harmaline) are reversible MAO-A inhibitors central to ayahuasca pharmacology.

classes.label: Pyrrolidinophenone
classes.description: Cathinones whose amine nitrogen is enclosed in a pyrrolidine ring, as in MDPV and α-PHP. Potent dopamine–norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors.

classes.label: Adamantane
classes.description: Compounds built on the rigid diamond-lattice adamantane cage, including the NMDA antagonists memantine and amantadine.

classes.label: Piperidine
classes.description: Six-membered saturated rings containing one nitrogen — one of the most common heterocycles in pharmacology. The anilidopiperidine opioids (fentanyl and relatives) are its most consequential psychoactive branch.

classes.label: Carbamate
classes.description: Esters of carbamic acid, historically important as sedative-hypnotics such as meprobamate and carisoprodol.

classes.label: Benzimidazole
classes.description: Fused benzene–imidazole heterocycles. In psychoactive chemistry the family matters chiefly as the parent of the nitazene opioids.

classes.label: Nitazene (zene)
classes.description: 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids first developed in the 1950s and re-emerging as novel synthetic opioids, several of which exceed fentanyl in potency. Extreme overdose risk.

classes.label: Nitazepyne
classes.description: Nitazene analogues in which the flexible ethylamine side chain is replaced by an azetidine or pyrrolidine ring, such as etonitazepyne. Potency remains in the nitazene range; the same extreme overdose caution applies.

classes.label: Nitazepipne
classes.description: Nitazene analogues carrying a piperidine ring in place of the ethylamine side chain, such as etonitazepipne. As with the parent nitazenes, potency and overdose risk are extreme.

classes.label: Indole
classes.description: The fused benzene–pyrrole ring system at the heart of serotonin and its mimics. The tryptamines — and through them the lysergamides, ibogalogs, and β-carbolines — are all elaborated indoles.

classes.label: Indazole
classes.description: Benzene fused to a pyrazole ring; a bioisostere of indole. Most visible in psychoactive chemistry as the core of many synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonists.

classes.label: Triazolobenzodiazepine
classes.description: Benzodiazepines fused with a triazole ring, which typically raises potency and shortens onset — alprazolam, triazolam, and the designer benzodiazepine clonazolam among them.

classes.label: Thienodiazepine
classes.description: Benzodiazepine bioisosteres in which the fused benzene ring is replaced by a thiophene ring. Pharmacologically they behave as classical benzodiazepines.

classes.label: Thienotriazolodiazepine
classes.description: Diazepines combining both the thiophene ring swap and the fused triazole, as in etizolam and brotizolam. They inherit the short onset and high potency of the triazolo family.

classes.label: 1,5-Benzodiazepine
classes.description: Positional isomers of the classical 1,4-benzodiazepines with the ring nitrogens at the 1- and 5-positions, exemplified by clobazam. Similar GABAergic pharmacology with a distinct side-effect profile.

classes.label: Cyclopyrrolone
classes.description: Non-benzodiazepine GABA-A positive modulators ('Z-drugs') built on a cyclopyrrolone core, including zopiclone and eszopiclone.

classes.label: Pyrazolopyrimidine
classes.description: Fused pyrazole–pyrimidine heterocycles; in psychoactive use, the Z-drug hypnotic zaleplon.

classes.label: Imidazopyridine
classes.description: Fused imidazole–pyridine heterocycles, most prominently the Z-drug hypnotic zolpidem.

classes.label: Isoxazole
classes.description: Five-membered rings containing adjacent oxygen and nitrogen atoms. Muscimol and ibotenic acid, the actives of Amanita muscaria, are its principal psychoactive members.

classes.label: Xanthine
classes.description: Purine-derived alkaloids including caffeine, theobromine, and theophylline — adenosine receptor antagonists and the most widely consumed stimulants on earth.

classes.label: Non-metal nitride
classes.description: Simple inorganic nitrogen compounds. Nitrous oxide, the classic dissociative anaesthetic gas, is the family's psychoactive representative.

classes.label: Noble gas
classes.description: Chemically inert monatomic gases. Xenon acts as an NMDA-antagonist anaesthetic at high partial pressures.

classes.label: Ether
classes.description: Compounds with an oxygen bridging two carbon groups. Diethyl ether was among the first anaesthetics and recreational depressants.

classes.label: Dibenzopyran
classes.description: The tricyclic ring system underlying the classical phytocannabinoids, including THC and CBD.

classes.label: Diphenylmethanethiol
classes.description: Sulfur-bearing benzhydryl compounds — the modafinil family of eugeroics (modafinil, armodafinil, and analogues such as flmodafinil).

classes.label: Diphenylmethanol
classes.description: Benzhydryl compounds built on a diphenyl-substituted carbinol carbon, including the ethanolamine antihistamines such as diphenhydramine.

classes.label: Alcohol
classes.description: Compounds bearing a hydroxyl group on a saturated carbon. Ethanol is the archetype; 2M2B and the alkanediols are less common relatives.

classes.label: Furanolactone
classes.description: Terpenoids carrying fused furan and lactone rings, most notably salvinorin A — the non-nitrogenous κ-opioid agonist of Salvia divinorum.
